Frozen copy /home/user/taskdeck/target/work/check-verify-e-read at bf10ef0, which is HEAD of W. Two things in W are not mine: W has uncommitted edits in command.rs, command/tests.rs and compile.rs, presumably the rulings writer's work in progress. They are not in the checked commit.

Step gate: exit 0 in the copy (cargo test, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, ci.sh, gate.sh purity-clippy-toml).

Import (src/legacy.rs, e1):
- Went through the fifteen steps of core.md §15.3 in order against the code. Sizes are checked before any parse. Parsers mirror today's Active, Session, Recurrence, Archived and Subscription (I compared fields and serde attributes in /home/user/taskdeck/src); ColorScheme is mirrored by LegacyScheme. Lines split at 0x0A; White_Space trim; non-UTF-8 lines kept as unreadable. Notes are detabbed. Plans migrate as today's migrate_legacy_plans. Step 9 renumbering: L, item, row and subscription order, 9.4 device-minted ids, and overflow listed per the lead's ruling. Kinds; sids numbered live items by ascending new id, then rows by line; instants; field and cap checks; notes-cap warning; marks; archive and unreadable order; check and the 61,865,984-byte cap.
- Probed by hand and confirmed: notes_unreadable and subscriptions_unreadable come before id_range; a row with id >= 2^62 gets next after the items; a leap second gives instant_range; 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999999999Z is accepted and the same time at -00:01 is refused; 21 subscriptions give field_range [21]; an unparsed line of 65,537 bytes gives cap and one of 65,536 is kept; home rounds half away from zero (0.005 gives 1, -0.005 gives -1); 90.005 gives the home_out_of_range warning.
- Worked two folders by hand and compared with what import returns:
  - fixtures/boards/small: no renumbering. sids 1,2 on item 3; 3,4,5 on item 14; 6 on item 16; 7 on row 23. Mark {0, item 34, block 7}. Archive order 27,24,23,25,26,28. Instants match the +02:00/+01:00 offsets. Palette is scheme 100; home is (-4125, -13250).
  - fixtures/legacy-other/small: six items with id 0 become 30..35. sids: item 14 gets 1, item 16 gets 2, item 30 gets 3 (ascending new id, not file order). Mark {0, 35, 3}. Three blocks come from planned_start (45/90/30). Notes have 3 tabs detabbed, 164 scalars. Palette is scheme 1. Counts equal that folder's MIGRATION.json entry.
- Checked by hand that the first four import.json byte cases (device-minted ids, id 0 and repeated ids, plans/kinds/sids, archive lines) and the failure cases are correct; I did not recompute any fixture board_sha256.
- The report holds no text: ImportReport has only integers, bools and enums, so it cannot carry a name, notes or a URL.

Read side (e2):
- Went through the fourteen differences of §14.3 in snapshot.rs. Compared field order and serde attributes of every snapshot type with today's phone.rs 2055-2346. The builders match today's build_day, build_tray, item_detail, done_rows and with_subscribed apart from the listed changes. ranked_ids and the tray sort stably over ascending id.
- The transform in tests/snapshot_fixtures.rs does only what §18.5 and §18.7 say: sort items, replace sids, rewrite archived_at canonically, add notes_base 0, take the palette, and handle the removed records of dst-edges.
- 48 json files are on disk. Not compared (5, exact list asserted): the Berlin 1970-01-01 dst-edges file and the two files each of id-limits and unreadable.
- The test is not vacuous. Mutations in my copy (all reverted) that it catches: notes_base+1 (43 of 43 differ); done not reversed (42/43); a corrupted archived_at (42/43); `when` hour+1 (42/43); reversed id tie order of entries (12/43).
- Two mutations survive the fixture test because no fixture covers them: ghost minutes without max(15), and skipping routine rows in archive_by_day. Unit tests in src/snapshot/tests.rs and src/read/tests.rs catch both.
- Worked all 8 reminders.json cases by hand (sources, leads, both window ends, (fire_at, key) order, key form, a fire_at before the instant range): all correct.
- Ported tests: all 6 of today's builder tests are in snapshot/tests.rs. zones.rs uses today's EU/US rules.
